speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information. To better understand your condition, could you please tell me what specific antibiotics you were taking and when you started taking them?

Also, can you describe the appearance of the itchy rash?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-induced morbilliform drug eruption.

This reaction is classic for amoxicillin hypersensitivity in children presenting with a rash in the flexural areas (antecubital and popliteal fossae) alongside fever and joint pain. Since the symptoms started one week after initiating the antibiotic, it is highly likely a delayed immune response to the medication. Please ensure the child stops the amoxicillin immediately and consults with a pediatrician for potential antihistamines or short-term steroids to manage the itching and inflammation.
